notes.summary: Reconstructed canonical geometric envelopes: greatest C/D existence iff raw continuity, with every-degree uniform convergence.
notes.detailedSummary: Relative to ENTIRE qualified G331's actual Cartier comparison, proves raw C and D suprema equal the all-support canonical primary supremum, continuity/attainment/uniform convergence equivalence and raw obstacle Lipschitz continuity. These are reconstructed foundations, not claimed new results; no source CE is inferred.
notes.text:
Let R be an excellent reduced local ring of positive dimension, a a proper primary ideal, and X=V_a(R), retaining every prime support. Throughout, C_R and D_R are precisely ENTIRE qualified G331's independently geometric classes. Their core uses actual negative effective FINITE REAL Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, with degree at least zero on EVERY contracted proper integral curve BEFORE comparison or limits. G331's geometric-to-ideal comparison, rather than a redefinition of positivity, is the premise used below.

For a finite continuous signed obstacle f define p_R(f)=sup{g in C_R:g<=f}, B=max(0,-min f), A_m={b in R:v(b)+mf(v)>=0 for EVERY v in X}, and h_m=-v(A_m)/m. Put A_0=R. The semivaluation axioms make A_m an ideal; it contains a^ceil(mB), and A_m A_l is contained in A_(m+l). Hence A_m is unit-or-primary. Every h_m is finite continuous and below f. When proper, its divisor -E_(A_m)/m on its ACTUAL primary blowup is negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on every contracted proper integral curve. Units give zero. The constant -B is a geometric competitor, so -B<=p_R(f)<=min(f,0).

We reconstruct the existing foundation p_R(f)=sup_m h_m=sup{g in D_R:g<=f}. For a C competitor, granted rational-profile uniform density followed by a small negative rational boundary shift gives a rational profile -v(I)/r<=f arbitrarily close from below. Its tests imply I contained in A_r, whence -v(I)/r<=h_r. Conversely each h_m is a C competitor. For a D competitor g=inf_i g_i<=f, the increasing directed open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover the compact section. Compactness and directedness select one index valid everywhere. The C function g_i-epsilon is below f and at least g-epsilon. This proves equality of the raw C and D suprema, including partial bottom, without asserting uniform convergence of the decreasing net.

Let M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(1<=r<=N) h_r. For m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, grading gives A_r^k A_1^s contained in A_m, hence h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m>=h_r-rM_1/m; the last inequality uses h_r<=0. Thus H_N-NM_1/m<=h_m<=p_R(f). Every degree converges pointwise to p_R(f). If p_R(f) is continuous, the increasing strict-test open sets {H_N>p_R(f)-epsilon} cover X and one N works globally; the displayed estimate proves uniform convergence in every degree. Conversely uniform convergence places the limit in the closed geometric cone C_R. A greatest D minorant must equal the raw supremum, which is lower semicontinuous as a supremum of continuous functions and upper semicontinuous as a D member, hence continuous. Therefore greatest C existence, greatest D existence, raw continuity and uniform canonical convergence are equivalent.

Subtracting epsilon from a competitor for either of two obstacles at uniform distance at most epsilon gives a competitor for the other. Consequently ||p_R(f)-p_R(f')||<=||f-f'||. This requires neither attainment nor source continuity.

All ENTIRE G331 qualifications remain attached: actual primary models only; no arbitrary-model cofinality, singular resolution, CM/QG, finite generation, algebraization or universal regular-cover premise; every support quotient field and infinite conductor fibre; nilpotent reduction and the empty dimension-zero boundary. notes.summary: New universal conductor obstruction between normalization centres, without source CE or finite regular covers.
notes.detailedSummary: For any excellent reduced local germ, arbitrary characteristic/residue field and all supports, a normalization fibre joining distinct local centres admits the explicit signed primary obstacle v((ce)+a^N)-N. The granted normal quantitative bound forces a negative conductor value, while actual positive conductor-primary minorants give raw value zero along a dense approaching net. Proves non-USC, no greatest C/D minorant, every-degree gap kappa=(N-nu(c))/A and perturbation gap kappa-2epsilon. USC regularization remains below the obstacle but is outside the SAME geometric D/C class. All conclusions are unverified draft mathematics relative to the qualified grant.
notes.text:
NEW SCOPED THEOREM. Let R be any positive-dimensional excellent REDUCED local ring, with arbitrary characteristic and residue field. Let S be its finite normalization, retaining EVERY normal local centre S_i above the marked maximal ideal. For a primary gauge a put Y=disjoint union of Y_i=V_(aS_i)(S_i), X=V_a(R), and let rho:Y->X be restriction. Suppose one full fibre contains w_i in Y_i and w_j in Y_j for DISTINCT centres i!=j. Then an explicit signed PRIMARY model obstacle has a non-upper-semicontinuous raw geometric envelope, no greatest C or D minorant, and a uniform positive gap in every canonical degree. No source envelope continuity, smoothness, or finite regular cover is assumed. The normal centres may themselves be singular and nonisolated.

PROOF. Write cfrak=(R:S) and choose a regular conductor element c, granted by ENTIRE qualified G331. Every S_i is an excellent normal local DOMAIN. Choose a normalized centred support-zero divisorial valuation nu on S_i, using G331 n6's qualified full-section divisorial density. Then d=nu(c) is finite. Choose an integer N>d, N>=1.

Choose e in S that is a unit at centre i and belongs to (aS_k)^N at every other centre k. To construct it, contract those local primary ideals to S. Their maximal radicals are distinct, so they and the maximal ideal at i are pairwise comaximal. Chinese remainder gives e congruent to 1 at i and to 0 modulo every other contracted primary ideal. This also works for distinct local centres on the same global normalization component; no separating global idempotent is presumed. Since cS is contained in R, ce belongs to R. Set I=(ce)+a^N and f(v)=v(I)-N.

The conductor cannot contain a unit of R when a normalization fibre is identified: a unit conductor element would give S=R. Thus c belongs to the maximal ideal and d>0. Since nu(e)=0, nu(I)=d<N; I is proper and contains a primary power, hence is actual primary. The obstacle f is a finite continuous signed difference of primary profiles, with -N<=f<=0. Its pullback F is zero on every Y_k with k!=i: there w(e)>=N and w(c)>=0, so w(I)=N, including infinite element values. At nu, F(nu)=d-N=-b, where b=N-d>0.

The precise quantitative inequality proved inside granted G331 n6 says that for this fixed normalized divisorial nu there is a finite A>=1 such that u(nu)>=A u(w) for EVERY u in C_(S_i) and EVERY w in Y_i. Its current application meets the exact hypotheses: S_i is excellent NORMAL local domain, its completion is analytically irreducible as qualified in the grant, and aS_i is primary. The normal nonunit divisorial order bound gives nu(J)<=A w(J) for primary ideals J; units are separately zero. Uniform comparison extends this to C. Enlarging A to at least one preserves the inequality because u<=0. Taking actual decreasing limits extends it to D, with A(-infinity)=-infinity and no infinity subtraction.

If g is any target C or D minorant of f, its pullback to S_i belongs to that same granted class. Since its value at nu is at most -b, the inequality forces its value at EVERY w in Y_i to be at most -b/A=-kappa. In particular, at v_*=rho(w_i)=rho(w_j), p_R(f)(v_*)<=-kappa<0. The full conductor value at v_* is infinite because G331 makes every finite-conductor fibre a singleton.

We construct ACTUAL positive primary minorants exhibiting the opposite limiting value from centre j. Granted semilocal primary/unit gluing supplies an ideal J of S with local ideal (aS_i)^N at i and the unit ideal at every other centre. Thus q(w)=-w(J) equals -N on Y_i and zero elsewhere, and q<=F. For every r>=1 define the actual downstairs ideal B_r=cfrak J^r+a^(Nr). The first summand is contained in R because the conductor is an S-ideal contained in R; it is finitely generated as an R-ideal by Noetherianity. Its extension to S is exactly the displayed sum. Finite ideal generators and nonnegative coefficients give, on EVERY support,

rho^*(-v(B_r)/r)(w)=max{q(w)-w(cfrak)/r,-N}.

At infinite conductor value the first term is minus infinity and the second survives. On Y_i this profile is -N<=F; on every other centre it is nonpositive and below F=0. Surjectivity therefore makes it a target minorant. Its value at rho(nu) is -N, so B_r is proper; it contains a^(Nr), hence is primary. On its ACTUAL primary blowup, -E_(B_r)/r is negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted proper integral curve BEFORE limits.

For w in Y_j of finite conductor value, these minorants tend to zero. Since all geometric competitors are nonpositive, p_R(f)(rho(w))=0 at every such point. This locus is dense in the full Y_j: the regular c is nonzero on that domain centre and has finite value at all support-zero divisorial points, and G331 n6 grants their full-section density with its Rees-DVR/dimension/historical qualifications. Choose a net of such points w_lambda->w_j. Its restrictions v_lambda tend to v_*, while p_R(f)(v_lambda)=0 and p_R(f)(v_*)<=-kappa. This is a non-USC jump of at least kappa. By own n1, greatest C and greatest D minorants do not exist.

Every actual D minorant g is USC and satisfies g(v_*)<=-kappa. Hence limsup g(v_lambda)<=-kappa, and sup_X(p_R(f)-g)>=kappa. In particular ||p_R(f)-h_m||>=kappa for EVERY canonical degree m. Bottom differences are interpreted as positive infinity. No uniform canonical convergence is possible.

Own n1's raw obstacle Lipschitz bound also proves stability without source CE. A continuous signed perturbation of size epsilon<kappa/2 has raw value at v_* at most -kappa+epsilon and values along the net at least -epsilon. It therefore retains a non-USC jump and every-minorant gap of at least kappa-2epsilon.

USC regularization cannot repair positivity. Define p^*(x)=inf_(open U containing x) sup_(z in U) p_R(f)(z). It is finite, USC and a majorant of p_R(f); continuity of f and p_R(f)<=f give p^*<=f. The zero-valued approaching net gives p^*(v_*)=0. The quantitative inequality above bounds p_R(f) by -kappa on the entire image of Y_i. The point x_0=rho(nu) has finite conductor value and belongs to no other centre image. Those other finitely many images are compact, hence closed, so a neighbourhood of x_0 meets only the image of Y_i. Thus p^*(x_0)<=-kappa. If p^* belonged to D_R, its pullback to S_i would satisfy the granted quantitative inequality, contradicting its zero value at w_i and negative value at nu. Consequently p^* is outside D_R and C_R. This is failure of positivity in the SAME independently geometric class, not a replacement cone or operator.

notes.text:
Use own n2's arbitrary excellent reduced setting. Define a finite incidence graph on the actual normal LOCAL CENTRES: i!=j are joined exactly when rho(Y_i) intersects rho(Y_j). By G331's full infinite-conductor rule, this is equivalent to two centred normalized semivaluations on the corresponding local conductor quotients restricting to the same semivaluation on R/cfrak. Every support and infinite-value quotient point is included. This is an intrinsic boundary test, not a claimed finite effective algorithm on rings.

Let CE(R) mean that every finite continuous signed obstacle on the full primary section has a greatest geometric C_R minorant. Own n1 proves equivalent definitions using greatest D_R minorants, raw continuity or uniform every-degree canonical convergence. Own n2 proves the NEW unconditional necessity:

CE(R) implies that the incidence graph has no edges.

There is no characteristic, smoothness, source-CE or regular-cover condition in this necessity.

NEW COMPLETE SCOPED CRITERION. Assume restriction rho|_(Y_i) is injective inside each individual local centre. Equivalently, the corresponding local conductor quotient restriction is injective on its entire normalized boundary; finite-conductor fibres are already singleton. Then

CE(R) iff [the incidence graph has no edges AND CE(S_i) holds at every normal local centre].

Proof: no edges together with internal injectivity makes rho a continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff full boundaries, hence a homeomorphism. G331's full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives an order isomorphism C_R with the finite product of C_(S_i), and likewise for D. An arbitrary continuous obstacle therefore corresponds to an arbitrary tuple of continuous obstacles, and raw and attained envelopes correspond componentwise. This proves both directions when there are no edges. An edge excludes CE(R) by own n2, proving the equivalence. Whenever the normal centres have CE, internal injectivity leaves precisely the intrinsic incidence test for target CE. No finite regular cover is presumed or constructed, and CE of the normal centres is not proved by this criterion.

The remaining case is explicit. Without internal injectivity, absence of graph edges does not decide identifications WITHIN a single centre. The zero-versus-negative centre separation used in n2 is then unavailable. General normal higher-dimensional nonisolated CE, higher-dimensional positive/mixed-characteristic regular-source CE and arbitrary same-centre conductor classification remain unresolved. This is a new complete scoped criterion and an original-residual bridge, not closure of the unchanged P12.3.

For a new primary ideal b put d(v)=v(b)>0. G331's exact homogeneous transport divides both obstacles and competitors by d(v), which is the same on every full normalization fibre. Taking suprema gives the same transport for raw and attained envelopes. Bounded continuous d and d^(-1) preserve CE and uniform convergence; graph incidence and internal injectivity are gauge independent. Along n2's approaching net d(v_lambda)->d(v_*), so its jump becomes kappa/d(v_*). The granted exact completion boundary homeomorphism and primary-ideal contraction transport the obstruction and CE predicate to completion. No model-category equivalence or generic-degree base-change assertion is made. Nilpotents first reduce away; a zero-dimensional local reduction has the unique empty boundary and empty envelope.

The curve comparison is reconstructed rather than claimed new. An excellent reduced curve has finitely many normal local DVR centres, each with singleton normalized section and finite conductor value. Normalization restriction is therefore a bijection of finite discrete links. Primary powers, unit profiles and positive real scaling give all finite nonpositive values at a DVR; actual decreasing constants give all extended nonpositive values. Semilocal gluing and G331's geometric POSITIVE descent give the downstairs geometric envelope P_R(f)=min(f,0), agreeing with the complete ideal-psh envelope. This conclusion uses the actual Cartier comparison, not merely ideal order calculus. The incidence graph has no edges, consistent with the obstruction theorem.
